Git is refusing to merge because the two branches have **no common commit**—Git can’t find a shared history to use as the merge base. This often happens when you’re combining two separately created repositories, or merging a branch with an orphaned history.

If you intended to combine them, you can allow it explicitly:

```bash
git merge <branch> --allow-unrelated-histories
```

Or, when pulling:

```bash
git pull <remote> <branch> --allow-unrelated-histories
```

This may produce conflicts. Before doing it, check that you have the right remote and branch; the flag permits a merge Git would otherwise block, but doesn’t make the histories related.
